topic: Dimensional Shifts: Bridging the 2D and 3D Divide in Geometry
target_audience: High school students interested in spatial reasoning and geometry

sections.title: The Flatland Limitation (0:00-0:45)
lecture_lines: Dimensions define our degree of movement.
Flatlanders perceive only length and width.
Depth remains hidden to a 2D world.
animations: 1. Fade in a 2D plane (Color #FFFFFF) representing the Flatland world.
2. Render a 2D square (Color #FF5733) moving across the plane.
3. Show a 3D circle (Color #33FF57) passing through the plane, appearing as a circle that grows and shrinks.

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Power of Projections (0:45-1:45)
lecture_lines: Silhouettes reveal aspects of hidden 3D depth.
animations: 1. Render a 3D cube (Color #3498DB) with visible edges.
2. Cast a 2D shadow (Color #555555) of the cube onto a plane.
3. Animate the cube rotating, showing the 2D shadow changing shape continuously.

sections.title: The Dimensional Shift Puzzle: The Tesseract (1:45-3:15)
lecture_lines: A 3D cube unfolds into a 2D cross.
This reveals the nature of higher dimensions.
animations: 1. Render a 3D cube (Color #3498DB) and show it unfolding into a 2D net (cross shape).
2. Render a 4D Tesseract projection (Color #E74C3C) using eight interconnected 3D cubes.
3. Animate the 3D 'net' of the Tesseract expanding or unfolding in 3D space.

sections.title: Practical Logic: Solving Dimensional Puzzles (3:15-4:15)
lecture_lines: Think of MRI scans capturing shapes.
animations: 1. Display a series of 2D cross-sections (circles) one by one on screen.
2. Gradually stack these cross-sections to reveal a 3D cone shape (Color #F1C40F).
3. Highlight the correspondence between a specific slice and the 3D object section.

sections.title: Summary and Conceptual Leap (4:15-5:00)
lecture_lines: Higher dimensions are found through invariants.
Expand your perspective to visualize dimensions.
animations: 2. Project the bird's shadow on a flat surface.
3. Animate the bird looking down at the shadow, emphasizing the difference in dimensionality.
